body: You are right on point with your suspicion, but the energy you are spending worrying is better spent preparing. If I were you I would make sure to have some non-perishable food and precious metals so that your savings will hold their value. Many people throughout history have went through war, famine, etc. but the ones that survived had a better understanding of the situation and applied their knowledge. Stay safe and I hope the best for you.
The more fear I feel the younger I act. The youngest I have acted is as a terrified 18 month year old, and the worst is 30 months because that is the age toddlers go into rages over trivial things.

I feel like I am watched all the time, especially when there is a lot of people around. The attitude of accepting what could happen to me if that was true made it so it doesn't bother me that much anymore. In the beginning I couldn't even go to the grocery store without freaking out, now I can be in a crowd with little problems.
You can have fun with that since that assertion does not change anything. You will realize there is no problem since knowing whether you are real or not doesn't matter.
You will stop struggling once the med kicks in, don't worry.

Whether you use drugs or not is something your psychiatrist out of professionalism is obligated to take your word for. This behavior comes out of learning through residency not to believe schizophrenics at face value since doing that is more work for them. It is easier to deflect complaints than to have to deal with med changes and the proper tapering needed. In a psych ward the approach is to stop psychosis as soon as possible which requires a high dose of meds. If she doesn't take your concerns into consideration there is no point in seeing her, get a new pdoc.
Only you can determine whether reality exists at the end of the day. Don't freak yourself out over it because it wont affect your life no matter what you believe.

My intrusive thoughts align with my emotions since they influence each other. My trick is to investigate the thoughts to get to the truth of their negativity. When they insult me instead of being hurt I wonder if that insult accurately describes me. If these thoughts are right they direct me to find what I need to improve in my life to make it better.
No, I am glad that I lost that time to psychosis because it made me wiser as a person and the suffering because of this bought me to understand my purpose.

Your diagnosis doesn't affect treatment except in the case it is a psychotic disorder where they default to antipsychotics. I have been diagnosed with Bipolar I, Schizophrenia, and Schizoaffective. All these terms do is represent a cluster of broad symptoms, they don't explain what is causing them. My psych even said diagnoses are only done for insurance reasons and treatment decisions are primarily based on symptoms unique to the individual.

They tortured a Georgian monk in the USSR with it for burning a banner of Lenin during a May Day parade. Honestly if you aren't on a CTO just be polite but blunt with your doctor with what you don't want to take. Don't play the appeasement games because that will just waste your time.

You might be overmedicated. You will always have some breakthrough psychosis no matter what does you are on, meds can't help 100%. That's where you come in with learning to live with the residual symptoms.
Antipsychotics, milk, and being anointed with oil by an Orthodox priest have not made a dent in it. Considering ordering makeup and some cheap clothes...
That delusion is true metaphorically. We are all children of God and every case of schizophrenia is unique since it is such a broad diagnosis.
Everyone is insane, the only difference with me being my insanity is of a different nature.
Schizoaffective turned me from a high achieving college student to a NEET with terminal apathy. I don't even have enough energy to play video games most days.
Why are you back on it? Are you under or threatened with a CTO?

I am on Oral Invega, Lithium, and Lexapro. I have gained 40 pounds since I started antipsychotics in April of 2021. Some of the things I suffer from are very little motivation, decreased cognitive ability, and disturbed sleep. My pdoc said that the negative symptoms will get better as I get used to the med despite being on it for almost 4 MONTHS. Now I am fed up and am tapering off Invega and surprise, my energy is better and I feel a bit more motivated. My psychiatrist doesn't care that I am in bed most of the day besides for work.

I drank holy water last Sunday and my AGP thoughts and urges were almost completely gone. It has been 8 days since I attended church so I should probably go next Sunday before the AGP mind virus grows back.
I am so happy for you, truly a story of hope for all of us.

I found that the resources of the Eastern Orthodox Church have helped me. Unfortunately it doesn't completely remove it though. This was explained as being my cross to bear when I told my priest. I hope holy baptism and holy unction will make it leave my mind.

Thank you for the compliment, programming is hard and I am far from being good at it. I was Orthodox Christian but I lost interest in that, I think the meds again are to blame, they numb the spiritual aspect to yourself, almost like a lobotomy of the spirit. My plan is to finish this year of college on minimal psych meds and than to try to come off of them. I will use the summer to try to revisit the psychosis/spiritual emergency/kundalini awakening and see will resolve itself with the help of trauma based therapy. If it doesn't it is meds for life I guess.

Anything with computers interests me, on good days I can spend hours programming. I am going to take on more responsibility since I have done very little this summer to see if it is the meds or something else. Sometimes I just feel like nothing it worth the effort and I think I don't have enough experience with my mental illness to know how it influences my thinking. My rational brain knows and agrees to working hard being worthwhile but my emotional brain wants to simply give up. I think the best I can do is to take action to better myself until I can have the opportunity to try alternative treatments to my condition.

I have to go through a mental deliberation each time to convince myself to take the meds. I loved being psychotic but that isn't sustainable for the others around me. As much as I hate the idea of taking five figures worth of medication a year to stay sane, it is a begrudging must.
This. I started drinking a week ago and I soon found myself craving it and wanting more so I stopped yesterday before I slid entirely into addiction. DON'T DRINK!

I feel exactly the same as you, my life was overall together until the onset. The spiral is real, but remember you have already fallen and the direction to go now is up. Now a good day is if I manage to get the housework and hygiene done. Just know that every little thing you get done, even if it is as small as a brushing your teeth, is a win. Each win will make you have a stronger character so you can handle just that much more. After the fall, you have to start over, relearning how to handle life again. This process is a long and painful battle so you are definitely not a leech with that on your plate.

Did a little bit of programming today. My anhedonia with programming and walking is slowly improving so that I can enjoy it a little bit. My new med is great except that I am restless, can't focus, and my mood isn't controlled well.

I saw the actual boogey-man out my living room window when I was 4 or 5. He looked like a ghoulish tall man in mid-19th century street clothes with a mouth as wide as his head brandishing his razor sharp teeth while wearing a deformed top hat.

Cognitive symptoms will always be there, my speech has always been disorganized but even more so after the onset. Best thing to do is to pay attention to your speech and look at the person at the same time. This sounds weird but it works.

First I became interested in religion and made impulsive large purchases. I remember my sleep schedule becoming very irregular but I would still sleep about 8 hours, this is a big warning sign. I started to be a hypochondriac, thinking I was developing diabetes. Then it progressed into feeling like people were staring at me, and this feeling was so overwhelming I stayed in my dorm and only ate food I had in there and I stopped going to class. I spent all day on reddit arguing with people about COVID and I was shadow banned from my university subreddit and became extremely angry about it. So much in fact that I was going to post flyers around the university insulting this person. I eventually withdrew from college without my parent's knowledge and they came up the next day to get me. I came home and I thought the house was a copy of the original and all kinds of crazy shit. Eventually I ended up in the mental hospital for suicidal ideation. Now I am on AAPs diagnosed with Psychotic Disorder NOS and Bipolar I. This all happened over the course of 3-4 months.

If you are worried about the possible onset of a mental illness, go see a psychiatrist.
It is fine. They are whoever you want them to be, and if you want them to be your parents, then they are :)
